answer: A market for comet observations and copper surveys in a delta lets each verified person authorize one agent ballot per round. An issuer checks liveness and deduplicates a canonical identity record before signing a credential. Each ballot proves that credential in zero knowledge and reveals a round-specific nullifier derived from its stable identifier; aliases and replacement credentials reuse the same nullifier and cannot vote twice. A farm must recruit more real people or defeat the issuer's checks. Credential lending and corrupt issuers remain risks; key uniqueness alone would not suffice.
